title: Representables of w-contractible affines are projective
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ w-contractible be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

1. Every epimorphism of sheaves of sets $F\to h_U$ has a section.
2. $h_U$ is projective in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})$: for every epimorphism $F\to G$, the map
   $F(U)\to G(U)$ is surjective.

proof.text: Apply the already proved source theorem [lem-weil-pbc-source-affine-wcontractible-evaluation] to the identity isomorphism of Spec D. This gives weak contractibility of U for Type (u+1)-valued sheaves. Its closed proof uses exactly the finite affine refinement, splitting of the coproduct cover, inverse-image disjoint clopen partition, and gluing route in this unit. No new geometric assertion is assumed.

For every epimorphism φ:F→G, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] makes φ locally surjective. The weak-contractibility conclusion from step 1 therefore makes φ_U surjective. This is clause 2, for arbitrary F and G and without any nonemptiness hypothesis.

For an epimorphism φ:F→h_U, apply the surjectivity from step 2 to id_U (with the universe lift). Let x be its preimage. The sheaf version of [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] sends x to a morphism s:h_U→F. Naturality of the Yoneda bijection in the sheaf identifies s≫φ with the identity because both evaluate to id_U. This proves clause 1, including the empty scheme. Mathlib already supplies subcanonicality of ProEt.topology, so det-pe-topos-functoriality-site is not needed.
